1	# EngiGraph: The Connected Digital Thread for Industrial Asset Management
2	## ER&I AI Innovation Challenge Submission
3	
4	**Version:** v3 | **Date:** 2026-02-20
5	**Submission deadline:** February 24, 2026
6	**Complementary Innovation:** ISHE (Industrial Semantic Harmonization Engine) — `docs/BUSINESS_CASE_v3.md`
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Q1. Innovation Title
11	
12	**EngiGraph: The Connected Digital Thread for Industrial Asset Management**
13	*Transforming Static Engineering Drawings into a Dynamic Knowledge Graph*
14	
15	> "Every industrial AI initiative needs two things: clean operational data and accurate engineering context. ISHE delivers clean data. EngiGraph delivers context — the knowledge of what assets exist, how they connect, and what the engineering drawings say about them."
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Q2. Problem Statement
20	
21	### The Heart of the Business Problem
22	
23	Industrial facilities run on engineering drawings. A large refinery typically operates with 2,000–10,000+ Piping and Instrumentation Diagram (P&ID) sheets, each encoding complete asset topology: every pipe, every valve, every instrument, every control loop, every safety interlock. These drawings are the authoritative engineering description of what exists in the plant and how it is connected.
24	
25	Today, they are static PDFs — "analog anchors" that trap engineering knowledge in a form machines cannot read. Consulted manually. Cross-referenced by eye. Frequently out of date.
26	
27	This is not merely an efficiency problem. It is a form of technical debt that actively constrains every downstream AI initiative. Every digital twin, predictive maintenance program, and AI copilot deployment that depends on engineering context must first resolve this debt before it can deliver value. Organizations that address the documentation layer systematically before deploying AI consistently outperform those that attempt to build on top of unresolved drawing libraries. EngiGraph eliminates this debt — converting analog anchors into a dynamic, machine-readable knowledge graph that makes all downstream AI viable.
28	
29	**Three documented failure modes drive the cost:**
30	
31	**1. Intensive Manual Effort**
32	
33	A maintenance engineer who needs to build an isolation procedure for pump P-101 must manually trace process lines across 5–10 P&ID sheets, cross-reference isometric drawings for physical routing, verify that the revision they are viewing is current, and compile the result by hand. Even for a single process unit, this mapping exercise can consume three to six months of engineering effort and remains highly prone to transcription error. McKinsey research found that knowledge workers spend an average of 1.8 hours per day — 9.3 hours per week — searching and gathering information [7]. A 2022 CADENAS survey of 100,000+ engineers found that nearly half spent 1+ hour per day searching for technical data [8]. More recent data suggests this burden is growing: the Coveo 2022 Workplace Relevance Report found knowledge workers now spend an average of 3.6 hours per day searching for information [17] — double the 2012 McKinsey estimate. In an engineering department supporting a major maintenance turnaround — where hundreds of contractors work simultaneously under time pressure — this information retrieval burden is a dominant cost driver and a direct contributor to overrun risk. Each day of turnaround overrun costs a large refinery $1M+ in deferred production [6].
34	
35	**2. Lack of Context: Fragmented Asset Information**
36	
37	A single physical asset — pump P-101 — appears across P&IDs, 3D models, isometric drawings, inspection reports, maintenance work orders, ERP functional locations, and SCADA/historian tags. None of these systems know about each other. The SCADA tag does not know which P&ID sheet it appears on. The inspection report does not reference the connected instruments. The ERP work order does not link to the P&ID revision that describes the current configuration.
38	
39	No single system holds the complete engineering picture of any asset. Every initiative that requires that picture — digital twin construction, HAZOP revalidation, AI-assisted maintenance planning — must manually assemble it from fragments. This is expensive, slow, and error-prone.
40	
41	**3. Data Accuracy and Revision Control**
42	
43	P&IDs are living documents. A major facility issues dozens of revisions per month. Distributing current revisions to all consuming parties — engineering teams, maintenance crews, contractor organizations — is a manual process that consistently lags. Engineers working from outdated P&IDs make decisions based on process configurations that no longer exist.
44	
45	Process safety authorities — including CCPS (Center for Chemical Process Safety) guidelines on management of change — consistently identify "wrong drawing / outdated revision" among the leading causal factors in maintenance-related process safety incidents [19]. IEC 61511 (Safety Instrumented Systems), IEC 61882 (HAZOP), and API 580/581 (Risk-Based Inspection) all require accurate, current P&ID data as the foundation for safety-critical decisions. Today, there is no mechanism to enforce currency across a distributed drawing library.
46	
47	**4. Platform Lock-in Risk: The Open Architecture Constraint**
48	
49	A structurally distinct demand segment compounds the three technical failure modes above: organizations that have adopted explicit open architecture policies and will not purchase proprietary industrial data platforms — Cognite CDF, Hexagon SmartPlant, AVEVA, or similar — regardless of capability. These clients may be large industrials with data sovereignty mandates, organizations with prior lock-in experiences, or post-M&A integrations spanning multiple vendor ecosystems where standardizing on any single proprietary platform is neither feasible nor acceptable.
50	
51	For this segment, the problem is not merely technical — it is organizational: they need a custom-built, client-owned solution on open standards, delivered by an SI. EngiGraph is SI-delivered, built on ISO 15926 / DEXPI open standards, and runs entirely in the client's own cloud tenant. No platform licensing. No data leaving the client environment. Full graph and data ownership on delivery. For these clients, EngiGraph is not competing with Cognite — the client has already ruled Cognite out. EngiGraph is the only viable path.
52	
53	### Cross-Sector Evidence
54	
55	The same three-failure-mode pattern is documented across three active engagements and four distinct industrial sectors:
56	
57	**Arkema (specialty chemicals):** Active OT harmonization study underway. As part of this engagement, Amazon Neptune has been recommended as the graph database foundation for connecting Arkema's P&ID topology to operational tag data — an architectural recommendation that directly maps to EngiGraph's knowledge graph approach. EngiGraph would productize and extend this into a full connected knowledge graph across the global Arkema facility portfolio.
58	
59	**Chevron (upstream O&G):** The $53B Hess Corporation acquisition brought an incompatible drawing library from Hess's Guyana and Bakken operations. Integrating those drawings into Chevron's asset management standards currently requires months of manual document review — before any digital twin, predictive maintenance, or autonomous operations initiative can proceed.
60	
61	**Active HAZOP and turnaround planning contexts (downstream and chemicals):** Multiple active client relationships confirm that manual P&ID tracing during HAZOP revalidation and turnaround isolation planning is among the highest-cost, highest-risk engineering activities. No existing tool automates it.
62	
63	### Sector-Specific Trigger Events
64	
65	| Sector | Trigger Event | The Problem |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| Upstream & Midstream O&G | M&A consolidation wave ($150B+ in 4 mergers within 12 months) brings incompatible drawing libraries | Drawing library integration requires months of manual review; digital twin and AI initiatives blocked until topology is resolved |
68	| Downstream & Chemicals | O-PAS/OPA migration requires clean P&ID topology as prerequisite; HAZOP revalidation cycles on 3–5 year intervals | Manual drawing review is the dominant cost driver in HAZOP; migration plans cannot proceed without knowing what connects to what |
69	| Power & Utilities | DER integration growing 20–30% annually — Wood Mackenzie projects the US DER market to nearly double 2022–2027, with solar capacity growing ~45% year-on-year in 2023–2024 [21]; each installation brings new single-line diagrams from OEM suppliers | CIM-compliant asset topology must be built from OEM drawings; manual extraction cannot keep pace with DER installation rates |
70	| Discrete Manufacturing | Industry 4.0 digital twin initiatives require accurate, queryable engineering documentation as the substrate | Digital twins without a machine-readable engineering context layer are 3D visualizations, not operational intelligence systems |
71	
72	### Impacted Clients, Personas, and Stakeholders
73	
74	| Persona | Role | Primary Pain Point |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| Process Engineer | Designs and modifies P&IDs; traces connections for design verification | Hours per task tracing connections manually; revision confusion when multiple P&ID revisions are in circulation simultaneously |
77	| Maintenance Engineer | Builds isolation procedures and Management of Change (MOC) documentation | Must manually traverse 5–10 P&ID sheets to build a single isolation list; no automated path-finding across connected equipment |
78	| Plant Operator | Executes procedures referencing drawings under field conditions | Cannot verify drawing currency in the field; works from potentially outdated revision |
79	| Turnaround Manager | Plans and executes major maintenance events involving hundreds of contractors | Drawing errors extend turnaround = $1M+/day in deferred production; isolation plan completeness is a safety-critical requirement |
80	| Process Safety Engineer | HAZOP, MOC, SIL verification, API 580/581 inspection planning | Manual drawing review for hazard analysis is slow, error-prone, and difficult to audit; no machine-readable record of review scope |
81	| CDO / Digital Lead | Governs enterprise engineering data; sponsors digital twin and AI initiatives | Digital twin and AI programs cannot proceed without a machine-readable asset topology; no single queryable source of truth exists |
82	| Document Control Manager | Manages drawing revisions across plant sites and contractor organizations | Distributed static files make revision control structurally unreliable; updates do not propagate automatically to consuming systems |
83	| Enterprise Architect / CTO with Open Architecture Mandate | Sets enterprise technology policy; approves or vetoes platform purchases | Has ruled out proprietary industrial platforms (Cognite, Hexagon, AVEVA) due to lock-in risk, data sovereignty requirements, or prior negative experiences; needs a custom-built, client-owned solution on open standards — EngiGraph's SI delivery model is the only path that satisfies this constraint |
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Q3. Expected Business Impact
88	
89	### Client Impact
90	
91	**Revenue Growth**
92	- Turnaround overrun risk directly monetizable: a refinery turnaround that overruns by one day costs $1M+[6]; accurate, current isolation plans derived from a knowledge graph — rather than manually assembled from drawings under time pressure — reduce that risk materially
93	- Digital twin enablement: EngiGraph provides the engineering context layer that makes digital twin investments viable; clients who have purchased Cognite CDF, AspenTech, AWS IoT TwinMaker, or similar platforms cannot extract value without a machine-readable engineering topology — which is what EngiGraph provides
94	- Engineering standards comparison: graph-powered comparison of "as-built" P&ID topology against engineering standards automatically identifies deviations — a high-value deliverable during M&A integration, commissioning, and periodic compliance audits where manual standards review currently requires months of engineering time
95	- Engineering cycle time reduction: HAZOP studies costing $500K–$2M+ per facility revalidation cycle — Kairos Technology (2021) benchmarks offshore HAZOPs at 5–20 MNOK depending on facility complexity [18] — can be compressed significantly with AI-assisted graph traversal replacing manual drawing review
96	
97	**Cost Reduction**
98	- Isolation procedure preparation: From 4–8 engineer-hours per isolation list (manual multi-sheet P&ID tracing) to <30 seconds (graph query) — representing 40–60% faster isolation planning and 90% reduction in isolation planning errors [16]; $50K–$200K in avoided labor per major turnaround *(internal estimate: 50–100 isolation lists per turnaround × 4–8 hours × $150/hr engineering rate)*; target ROI payback: 18 months [16]
99	- Engineering documentation processing: Similar AI-assisted P&ID extraction implementations have demonstrated 70–80% reduction in time required to process engineering documentation libraries [16] — replacing months of manual digitization with weeks of automated extraction
100	- Drawing search elimination: Eliminating 50% of drawing search effort in a 60-person engineering department saves ~27 engineer-hours per day → ~$1.5M annually in avoided labor *(internal projection based on McKinsey 1.8 hrs/day information search benchmark [7] × 60 engineers × $150/hr)*
101	- Manual P&ID digitization projects: Existing manual digitization programs (large SIs billing $5–20M over 12–24 months to digitize a drawing library by hand) replaced by a 4–8 week AI-assisted extraction — 60–80% cost reduction by the 5th engagement in a sector
102	
103	**Risk Mitigation**
104	- Eliminates "wrong drawing / outdated revision" as a causal factor in maintenance-related process safety incidents — the graph enforces single authoritative revision; no stale copies in distribution
105	- IEC 61511 Safety Instrumented System integrity: SIS boundary data maintained as a structured, version-controlled, auditable graph — not a set of distributed PDF files
106	- API 580/581 Risk-Based Inspection: Accurate P&ID topology as the foundation for inspection planning, queryable programmatically by inspection management systems
107	- MOC scope completeness: Graph change detection automatically identifies all downstream systems affected by a process change, ensuring MOC scope does not miss connected equipment
108	
109	**Experience Improvement**
110	- Process engineers and maintenance engineers describe manual P&ID tracing as among the most tedious and error-prone parts of their role — EngiGraph eliminates it for common tasks

395	### ISO 15926 Alignment and Multi-Level Ontology Architecture
396	
397	ISO 15926 is the international standard for "integration of life-cycle data for process plants including oil and gas production facilities" [12]. It defines a formal ontology for process plant assets using W3C Semantic Web technologies (RDF/OWL/SPARQL). EngiGraph uses it as the ontology foundation because: (1) it is the recognized O&G lifecycle data standard — ensuring regulatory defensibility; (2) the DEXPI extension provides a P&ID-specific schema that reduces ontology design work in the POC; (3) Hexagon SmartPlant, Bentley OpenPlant, and AVEVA all have ISO 15926 / DEXPI compatibility roadmaps.
398	
399	**Multi-level ontology architecture** — built following the "Sustainable Extensibility" principle, delivering value at each layer before the next is added:
400	
401	| Level | Scope | Content |

# EngiGraph: The Connected Digital Thread for Industrial Asset Management
## ER&I AI Innovation Challenge Submission

**Version:** v3 | **Date:** 2026-02-20
**Submission deadline:** February 24, 2026
**Complementary Innovation:** ISHE (Industrial Semantic Harmonization Engine) — `docs/BUSINESS_CASE_v3.md`

---

## Q1. Innovation Title

**EngiGraph: The Connected Digital Thread for Industrial Asset Management**
*Transforming Static Engineering Drawings into a Dynamic Knowledge Graph*

> "Every industrial AI initiative needs two things: clean operational data and accurate engineering context. ISHE delivers clean data. EngiGraph delivers context — the knowledge of what assets exist, how they connect, and what the engineering drawings say about them."

---

## Q2. Problem Statement

### The Heart of the Business Problem

Industrial facilities run on engineering drawings. A large refinery typically operates with 2,000–10,000+ Piping and Instrumentation Diagram (P&ID) sheets, each encoding complete asset topology: every pipe, every valve, every instrument, every control loop, every safety interlock. These drawings are the authoritative engineering description of what exists in the plant and how it is connected.

Today, they are static PDFs — "analog anchors" that trap engineering knowledge in a form machines cannot read. Consulted manually. Cross-referenced by eye. Frequently out of date.

This is not merely an efficiency problem. It is a form of technical debt that actively constrains every downstream AI initiative. Every digital twin, predictive maintenance program, and AI copilot deployment that depends on engineering context must first resolve this debt before it can deliver value. Organizations that address the documentation layer systematically before deploying AI consistently outperform those that attempt to build on top of unresolved drawing libraries. EngiGraph eliminates this debt — converting analog anchors into a dynamic, machine-readable knowledge graph that makes all downstream AI viable.

**Three documented failure modes drive the cost:**

**1. Intensive Manual Effort**

A maintenance engineer who needs to build an isolation procedure for pump P-101 must manually trace process lines across 5–10 P&ID sheets, cross-reference isometric drawings for physical routing, verify that the revision they are viewing is current, and compile the result by hand. Even for a single process unit, this mapping exercise can consume three to six months of engineering effort and remains highly prone to transcription error. McKinsey research found that knowledge workers spend an average of 1.8 hours per day — 9.3 hours per week — searching and gathering information [7]. A 2022 CADENAS survey of 100,000+ engineers found that nearly half spent 1+ hour per day searching for technical data [8]. More recent data suggests this burden is growing: the Coveo 2022 Workplace Relevance Report found knowledge workers now spend an average of 3.6 hours per day searching for information [17] — double the 2012 McKinsey estimate. In an engineering department supporting a major maintenance turnaround — where hundreds of contractors work simultaneously under time pressure — this information retrieval burden is a dominant cost driver and a direct contributor to overrun risk. Each day of turnaround overrun costs a large refinery $1M+ in deferred production [6].

**2. Lack of Context: Fragmented Asset Information**

A single physical asset — pump P-101 — appears across P&IDs, 3D models, isometric drawings, inspection reports, maintenance work orders, ERP functional locations, and SCADA/historian tags. None of these systems know about each other. The SCADA tag does not know which P&ID sheet it appears on. The inspection report does not reference the connected instruments. The ERP work order does not link to the P&ID revision that describes the current configuration.

No single system holds the complete engineering picture of any asset. Every initiative that requires that picture — digital twin construction, HAZOP revalidation, AI-assisted maintenance planning — must manually assemble it from fragments. This is expensive, slow, and error-prone.

**3. Data Accuracy and Revision Control**

P&IDs are living documents. A major facility issues dozens of revisions per month. Distributing current revisions to all consuming parties — engineering teams, maintenance crews, contractor organizations — is a manual process that consistently lags. Engineers working from outdated P&IDs make decisions based on process configurations that no longer exist.

Process safety authorities — including CCPS (Center for Chemical Process Safety) guidelines on management of change — consistently identify "wrong drawing / outdated revision" among the leading causal factors in maintenance-related process safety incidents [19]. IEC 61511 (Safety Instrumented Systems), IEC 61882 (HAZOP), and API 580/581 (Risk-Based Inspection) all require accurate, current P&ID data as the foundation for safety-critical decisions. Today, there is no mechanism to enforce currency across a distributed drawing library.

**4. Platform Lock-in Risk: The Open Architecture Constraint**

A structurally distinct demand segment compounds the three technical failure modes above: organizations that have adopted explicit open architecture policies and will not purchase proprietary industrial data platforms — Cognite CDF, Hexagon SmartPlant, AVEVA, or similar — regardless of capability. These clients may be large industrials with data sovereignty mandates, organizations with prior lock-in experiences, or post-M&A integrations spanning multiple vendor ecosystems where standardizing on any single proprietary platform is neither feasible nor acceptable.

For this segment, the problem is not merely technical — it is organizational: they need a custom-built, client-owned solution on open standards, delivered by an SI. EngiGraph is SI-delivered, built on ISO 15926 / DEXPI open standards, and runs entirely in the client's own cloud tenant. No platform licensing. No data leaving the client environment. Full graph and data ownership on delivery. For these clients, EngiGraph is not competing with Cognite — the client has already ruled Cognite out. EngiGraph is the only viable path.

### Cross-Sector Evidence

The same three-failure-mode pattern is documented across three active engagements and four distinct industrial sectors:

**Arkema (specialty chemicals):** Active OT harmonization study underway. As part of this engagement, Amazon Neptune has been recommended as the graph database foundation for connecting Arkema's P&ID topology to operational tag data — an architectural recommendation that directly maps to EngiGraph's knowledge graph approach. EngiGraph would productize and extend this into a full connected knowledge graph across the global Arkema facility portfolio.

**Chevron (upstream O&G):** The $53B Hess Corporation acquisition brought an incompatible drawing library from Hess's Guyana and Bakken operations. Integrating those drawings into Chevron's asset management standards currently requires months of manual document review — before any digital twin, predictive maintenance, or autonomous operations initiative can proceed.

**Active HAZOP and turnaround planning contexts (downstream and chemicals):** Multiple active client relationships confirm that manual P&ID tracing during HAZOP revalidation and turnaround isolation planning is among the highest-cost, highest-risk engineering activities. No existing tool automates it.

### Sector-Specific Trigger Events

| Sector | Trigger Event | The Problem |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream & Midstream O&G | M&A consolidation wave ($150B+ in 4 mergers within 12 months) brings incompatible drawing libraries | Drawing library integration requires months of manual review; digital twin and AI initiatives blocked until topology is resolved |
| Downstream & Chemicals | O-PAS/OPA migration requires clean P&ID topology as prerequisite; HAZOP revalidation cycles on 3–5 year intervals | Manual drawing review is the dominant cost driver in HAZOP; migration plans cannot proceed without knowing what connects to what |
| Power & Utilities | DER integration growing 20–30% annually — Wood Mackenzie projects the US DER market to nearly double 2022–2027, with solar capacity growing ~45% year-on-year in 2023–2024 [21]; each installation brings new single-line diagrams from OEM suppliers | CIM-compliant asset topology must be built from OEM drawings; manual extraction cannot keep pace with DER installation rates |
| Discrete Manufacturing | Industry 4.0 digital twin initiatives require accurate, queryable engineering documentation as the substrate | Digital twins without a machine-readable engineering context layer are 3D visualizations, not operational intelligence systems |

### Impacted Clients, Personas, and Stakeholders

| Persona | Role | Primary Pain Point |
|---|---|---|
| Process Engineer | Designs and modifies P&IDs; traces connections for design verification | Hours per task tracing connections manually; revision confusion when multiple P&ID revisions are in circulation simultaneously |
| Maintenance Engineer | Builds isolation procedures and Management of Change (MOC) documentation | Must manually traverse 5–10 P&ID sheets to build a single isolation list; no automated path-finding across connected equipment |
| Plant Operator | Executes procedures referencing drawings under field conditions | Cannot verify drawing currency in the field; works from potentially outdated revision |
| Turnaround Manager | Plans and executes major maintenance events involving hundreds of contractors | Drawing errors extend turnaround = $1M+/day in deferred production; isolation plan completeness is a safety-critical requirement |
| Process Safety Engineer | HAZOP, MOC, SIL verification, API 580/581 inspection planning | Manual drawing review for hazard analysis is slow, error-prone, and difficult to audit; no machine-readable record of review scope |
| CDO / Digital Lead | Governs enterprise engineering data; sponsors digital twin and AI initiatives | Digital twin and AI programs cannot proceed without a machine-readable asset topology; no single queryable source of truth exists |
| Document Control Manager | Manages drawing revisions across plant sites and contractor organizations | Distributed static files make revision control structurally unreliable; updates do not propagate automatically to consuming systems |
| Enterprise Architect / CTO with Open Architecture Mandate | Sets enterprise technology policy; approves or vetoes platform purchases | Has ruled out proprietary industrial platforms (Cognite, Hexagon, AVEVA) due to lock-in risk, data sovereignty requirements, or prior negative experiences; needs a custom-built, client-owned solution on open standards — EngiGraph's SI delivery model is the only path that satisfies this constraint |

---

## Q3. Expected Business Impact

### Client Impact

**Revenue Growth**
- Turnaround overrun risk directly monetizable: a refinery turnaround that overruns by one day costs $1M+[6]; accurate, current isolation plans derived from a knowledge graph — rather than manually assembled from drawings under time pressure — reduce that risk materially
- Digital twin enablement: EngiGraph provides the engineering context layer that makes digital twin investments viable; clients who have purchased Cognite CDF, AspenTech, AWS IoT TwinMaker, or similar platforms cannot extract value without a machine-readable engineering topology — which is what EngiGraph provides
- Engineering standards comparison: graph-powered comparison of "as-built" P&ID topology against engineering standards automatically identifies deviations — a high-value deliverable during M&A integration, commissioning, and periodic compliance audits where manual standards review currently requires months of engineering time
- Engineering cycle time reduction: HAZOP studies costing $500K–$2M+ per facility revalidation cycle — Kairos Technology (2021) benchmarks offshore HAZOPs at 5–20 MNOK depending on facility complexity [18] — can be compressed significantly with AI-assisted graph traversal replacing manual drawing review

**Cost Reduction**
- Isolation procedure preparation: From 4–8 engineer-hours per isolation list (manual multi-sheet P&ID tracing) to <30 seconds (graph query) — representing 40–60% faster isolation planning and 90% reduction in isolation planning errors [16]; $50K–$200K in avoided labor per major turnaround *(internal estimate: 50–100 isolation lists per turnaround × 4–8 hours × $150/hr engineering rate)*; target ROI payback: 18 months [16]
- Engineering documentation processing: Similar AI-assisted P&ID extraction implementations have demonstrated 70–80% reduction in time required to process engineering documentation libraries [16] — replacing months of manual digitization with weeks of automated extraction
- Drawing search elimination: Eliminating 50% of drawing search effort in a 60-person engineering department saves ~27 engineer-hours per day → ~$1.5M annually in avoided labor *(internal projection based on McKinsey 1.8 hrs/day information search benchmark [7] × 60 engineers × $150/hr)*
- Manual P&ID digitization projects: Existing manual digitization programs (large SIs billing $5–20M over 12–24 months to digitize a drawing library by hand) replaced by a 4–8 week AI-assisted extraction — 60–80% cost reduction by the 5th engagement in a sector

**Risk Mitigation**
- Eliminates "wrong drawing / outdated revision" as a causal factor in maintenance-related process safety incidents — the graph enforces single authoritative revision; no stale copies in distribution
- IEC 61511 Safety Instrumented System integrity: SIS boundary data maintained as a structured, version-controlled, auditable graph — not a set of distributed PDF files
- API 580/581 Risk-Based Inspection: Accurate P&ID topology as the foundation for inspection planning, queryable programmatically by inspection management systems
- MOC scope completeness: Graph change detection automatically identifies all downstream systems affected by a process change, ensuring MOC scope does not miss connected equipment

**Experience Improvement**
- Process engineers and maintenance engineers describe manual P&ID tracing as among the most tedious and error-prone parts of their role — EngiGraph eliminates it for common tasks
- Turnaround managers gain confidence in isolation plan completeness before crews enter the field; safety-critical errors caught before they cost downtime
- CDOs and digital leads gain the engineering context layer needed to operationalize investments in Cognite, AspenTech, AWS IoT, and similar platforms
- Safety engineers gain machine-readable, auditable HAZOP support that reduces study preparation time and improves review completeness
- The human+AI architecture of EngiGraph — engineers validate extractions; GraphRAG grounds all AI query responses in verified graph data — reflects the consistent pattern in industrial AI programs that the highest returns come from workflows combining machine speed with human engineering judgment, not from full automation alone

### Scale Potential for the Firm

| Asset Integrity Management market | $25–31B in 2025 [2] (range across analysts: MarketsandMarkets $25.07B; Business Research Company $31.49B); growing at 5–7% CAGR to 2030 [3] |
| Digital Twin market (industrial) | $21B in 2025 → $150B by 2030 at 47.9% CAGR [4] |
| Plant Design Software market | ~$4.2B in 2024; growing at 6.5–10% CAGR [1] |
| EngiGraph TAM (engineering context layer) | $3–7B annually — internally derived; targets the AI-assisted extraction and knowledge graph construction layer embedded within AIM, plant design, and digital twin programs |
| Year 1 revenue | $7–14M (2–4 engagements; building the ontology library) |
| Year 4 revenue | $40–70M+ (18–30 engagements; 70–80% ontology reuse; platform licensing upside) |
| Active cross-sector demand signal | Arkema (active OT harmonization study; Neptune-based architecture recommended), Chevron (M&A drawing library integration), downstream chemicals (HAZOP + turnaround planning) |

The firm that builds a defensible, compounding P&ID ontology library in the next 24 months will be positioned as the foundational engineering context layer for industrial AI for the next decade. A Year 4 revenue target of $40–70M represents <2% of the estimated TAM — a conservative share for a specialized, differentiated capability at market entry.

**ISHE + EngiGraph bundled TAM:** When positioned as a combined offering alongside ISHE (SCADA tag harmonization), the total addressable opportunity expands to $7.5–17B annually — the combined market for operational data harmonization (ISHE TAM: $4.5–10B [15]) and engineering context layer (EngiGraph TAM: $3–7B). Every industrial AI initiative requires both; neither is useful at full scale without the other.

### Likely Client Count (Conservative Scale View)

Based on active engagement patterns across the last 60 days:

---

## Q4. Proposed AI Solution

### Trigger

A maintenance turnaround, HAZOP revalidation, M&A drawing library integration, or digital twin initiative exposes the absence of a machine-readable engineering context layer. Engineers are manually searching, cross-referencing, and verifying drawings — work that should be automated.

### Architecture: Five-Layer Pipeline

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LAYER 1 — DATA SOURCES                                              │
│  PDFs · TIFFs · CAD files · DMS APIs · ERP exports                  │
│  P&IDs · Isometric Drawings · Inspection Reports · Revision History  │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
                             ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LAYER 2 — DATA ACQUISITION                                          │
│  Document collection · Metadata extraction · Version control         │
│  Pre-processing: image enhancement, format normalization,            │
│  quality assessment, sheet boundary detection                        │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
                             ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LAYER 3 — AI PROCESSING                                             │
│  ┌─────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  NLP / NLU / NLG    │    │  Entity & Relationship Extraction │    │
│  │  Query interpretation│    │  Symbol detection (ISA 5.1 CV)   │    │
│  │  Report generation  │    │  Advanced OCR + VLM               │    │
│  └─────────────────────┘    │  Spatial topology analysis        │    │
│                             │  Cross-sheet linking              │    │
│                             │  Confidence scoring               │    │
│                             └──────────────────────────────────┘    │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
                             ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LAYER 4 — SCHEMA & ONTOLOGY → KNOWLEDGE GRAPH                      │
│  ISO 15926 / DEXPI P&ID ontology [12]                               │
│  Nodes: Equipment · Instruments · Valves · Pipes · Control Systems  │
│  Edges: connects-to · controls · isolates · inspects · belongs-to   │
│  Amazon Neptune / Neo4j (billions of nodes and relationships)        │
└────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
                             ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LAYER 5 — APPLICATION + INTEGRATION LAYER                          │
│  Engineer-facing NL query interface                                  │
│  REST / GraphQL API → SmartPlant · Polarion · AspenTech             │
│  Cognite CDF · Kongsberg C3 · Aviva · SAP PM · IBM Maximo           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Steps → Output → User Value

| Step | Activity | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Document Ingestion | Collect P&IDs and drawings from DMS, SharePoint, or direct upload; extract sheet metadata (drawing number, revision, date, plant unit) |
| 2 | Pre-Processing | Image enhancement for scanned drawings; format normalization; quality assessment; sheet boundary detection for cross-sheet linking |
| 3 | Symbol Detection | Computer vision model (YOLO v8 / SAM 2 fine-tuned on ISA 5.1 library) identifies equipment and instrument symbols and their bounding boxes |
| 4 | Entity Extraction | VLM (Claude 3.7 Sonnet / GPT-4V) reads drawing callouts, tag labels, line numbers, annotations; extracts structured entities with confidence scores; VLMs achieve text similarity scores 3–4x higher than traditional OCR on complex documents [24], with P&ID-specific benchmarks showing F1 scores of 0.44–0.52 [23] — the first technology to deliver commercially viable extraction accuracy on engineering drawings |
| 5 | Relationship Extraction | Spatial topology analysis traces connecting lines; infers process flow direction; follows match lines across sheet boundaries |
| 6 | Ontology Mapping | Entities mapped to ISO 15926 / DEXPI classes; relationships assigned to standardized edge types; low-confidence items routed to engineer review queue |
| 7 | Graph Population | Nodes and edges written to Amazon Neptune or Neo4j; version control preserves prior graph states; change detection identifies added / modified / deleted entities vs. prior revision |
| 8 | Query & Integration | GraphRAG-powered query interface: graph is queried first; LLM composes response from retrieved graph data — not from general training data; eliminates hallucination risk for safety-critical queries; REST API for enterprise system integration; revision-change notifications propagate to subscribing applications |

**Outputs:**
- Structured knowledge graph: complete facility engineering topology, queryable by any node or relationship type
- Isolation valve list for any equipment tag — generated in <30 seconds via graph algorithms: shortest-path (isolation routes), centrality analysis (critical isolation points), impact analysis (all upstream/downstream affected components); 90% reduction in isolation errors vs. manual [16]
- Engineering standards comparison report — graph query compares "as-built" topology against standards; deviations identified automatically; applicable to M&A integration and compliance audits
- Instrument loop report for any control loop — all connected instruments, piping, and control functions
- P&ID revision change log — automatically generated delta between drawing revisions; structured list of added, modified, deleted entities
- Asset relationship export (JSON-LD / RDF) — compatible with Cognite CDF, digital twin platforms, and enterprise systems
- Engineer review queue — confidence-scored extractions below threshold, routed for targeted human validation

**User value by persona:**

| Persona | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Process Engineer | Hours tracing connections across multiple P&ID sheets | Graph query returns all connected assets in <30 seconds; graph is always current |
| Maintenance Engineer | Manual isolation list from 5–10 sheets, 4–8 hours per list | "Generate isolation list for P-101" → complete, auditable list in <30 seconds |
| Plant Operator | Cannot verify drawing currency in the field | Graph enforces single authoritative revision; version ambiguity eliminated |
| Turnaround Manager | Drawing errors extend turnaround = $1M+/day cost | Isolation plans validated against current graph before execution; errors caught before they cause overruns |
| Process Safety Engineer | Manual HAZOP drawing review; slow, difficult to audit | Graph traversal enumerates hazard propagation paths automatically; review is machine-assisted and auditable |
| CDO / Digital Lead | Digital twin blocked by absence of machine-readable topology | Graph is the engineering context layer for all downstream AI and analytics initiatives |
| Document Control Manager | Revision distribution is manual and unreliable | Graph auto-updates when drawings change; consuming systems notified automatically |

### Compounding Advantage

Like ISHE's semantic tag library, EngiGraph's ontology library is a compounding asset. Each P&ID set ingested improves symbol recognition models, enriches relationship pattern libraries, and extends sector-specific ontology coverage. By the 5th engagement in a given sector, extraction accuracy is 60–80% self-sustaining with minimal human correction.

| Engagement | Drawing Sheets | Ontology Growth | Extraction Reuse on Next Engagement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Client 1 (Downstream O&G) | 2,000 sheets | Baseline established | — |
| Client 2 (Specialty Chemicals) | 1,500 sheets | +300 entity patterns | ~65% |
| Client 3 (Upstream O&G) | 800 sheets | +150 wellhead patterns | ~70% |

The competitive landscape reveals a persistent and exploitable gap. ### ISO 15926 Alignment and Multi-Level Ontology Architecture

ISO 15926 is the international standard for "integration of life-cycle data for process plants including oil and gas production facilities" [12]. It defines a formal ontology for process plant assets using W3C Semantic Web technologies (RDF/OWL/SPARQL). EngiGraph uses it as the ontology foundation because: (1) it is the recognized O&G lifecycle data standard — ensuring regulatory defensibility; (2) the DEXPI extension provides a P&ID-specific schema that reduces ontology design work in the POC; (3) Hexagon SmartPlant, Bentley OpenPlant, and AVEVA all have ISO 15926 / DEXPI compatibility roadmaps.

**Multi-level ontology architecture** — built following the "Sustainable Extensibility" principle, delivering value at each layer before the next is added:

| Level | Scope | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Level 1 — Core Equipment | Single drawing set | Basic equipment taxonomy; simple CONNECTS_TO / CONTROLS / MEASURES relationships; document-to-entity associations |
| Level 2 — Process System | Single plant unit | Process flow (upstream/downstream); control loop associations; safety instrumentation relationships; full ISA 5.1 classification |
| Level 3 — Facility Integration | Full site | Cross-unit connectivity; FLOC hierarchy; inspection history; ERP work order linkage |
| Level 4 — Cross-Facility | Enterprise | Multi-site standardization; M&A drawing rationalization; engineering standards compliance mapping |

### Connection to ISHE — Sister Innovation Synergy

EngiGraph and ISHE address two halves of the same foundational problem for industrial AI:

| | ISHE | EngiGraph |
|---|---|---|
| **What it solves** | Operational data layer: SCADA tags are cryptic, inconsistent, machine-unreadable | Engineering context layer: P&IDs are static files, not queryable data |
| **Input** | SCADA tag libraries (CygNet, Wonderware, Ignition, FactoryTalk) | Engineering drawing libraries (P&IDs, isometrics, inspection reports) |
| **Output** | Canonical, ISA-95-aligned operational data with per-field lineage | Knowledge graph of assets, connections, and relationships |
| **What it unlocks** | Predictive maintenance, autonomous operations, GenAI copilots | Digital twins, HAZOP automation, isolation planning, digital thread |
| **Together** | Clean operational data (ISHE) + accurate engineering context (EngiGraph) = complete industrial AI foundation |

The combined offering is commercially differentiated because: (a) every industrial AI initiative requires both layers; (b) neither layer is useful at full scale without the other; and (c) switching costs apply to both layers simultaneously, creating durable client relationships that are difficult to displace.

Now I have the full picture of both folders, and the extraction is actually cleaner than I expected — because **EngiGraph *is* the knowledge-graph contextualization layer** your `design/` notes keep saying you'll eventually need (the Neo4j side). Here's what I'd pull from each, and just as importantly, what I'd leave behind.

## The unifying realization

Your two `docs` folders aren't random slices — they're the **two halves of contextualization** that the home-lab vision explicitly calls for, and the business cases say so themselves:

> *"ISHE delivers clean data. EngiGraph delivers context… Together = complete industrial AI foundation."*

Mapped onto your `design/` home-lab:

| `design/` home-lab layer | What feeds it | Source folder |
|---|---|---|
| Harmonization (PLC tag → Sparkplug metric, units, status, lineage) | **ISHE** technical model | `docs/` |
| Knowledge-graph contextualization (Neo4j: asset↔tag↔event↔work-order) | **EngiGraph** ontology + graph model | `engineering_drawing_business_case/` |
| Enterprise records (ERPNext) | both (curated events / FLOC linkage) | both |

So this isn't "bringing in a side project" — it's recognizing that ISHE + EngiGraph are the *operational* and *engineering* context halves of the single contextualization story in `uns_home_lab_notes.md`.

---

## Extract from `docs/` (ISHE) — the harmonization engine, technical layer

These are concrete, buildable artifacts that drop almost directly into the home-lab's harmonization layer (the `synthetic_data_generation` 6-layer pipeline, especially layers 3–4):

1. **The canonical Pydantic model hierarchy** (`ARCHITECTURE.md §2`, `PRD §5.3`) — `CanonicalTelemetry` → equipment-class submodels, `DataQuality`, `FieldLineage`, `DeadLetterEntry`, `UNSEnvelope`, `BirthCertificate`. This is exactly the "stage 3" semantic target of your three-stage mapping table.
2. **The ISA-95 identity model** (Enterprise→Site→Area→Cell→EquipmentClass→EquipmentID) — *generalize it* from O&G Well/ESP to the manufacturing Site/Area/Line/Cell/Asset hierarchy your home-lab uses. The structure transfers; only the example assets change.
3. **The three-stage mapping discipline** — ISHE's `source key → normalized field → canonical field + lineage` is the same spine as your home-lab's `friendly var → PLC tag → Sparkplug metric`. ISHE's `FieldLineage` and config-driven YAML mapping (M8) is a ready-made implementation of it.
4. **Transform primitives** — unit conversion, status normalization (→enum, unmapped→Unknown), timestamp coercion, data-quality flagging. Reusable verbatim.
5. **UNS *semantics*** — retained state, report-by-exception, birth certificates, wildcard matching, topic sanitization. ISHE implemented these in-memory; your home-lab does the *real* version over MQTT/Sparkplug B. ISHE is the **reference spec / test oracle** for what the real broker should do. (Note: ISHE's PRD explicitly lists "Sparkplug B / Protobuf" as a *non-goal* — the home-lab is precisely the project that closes that gap.)
6. **The milestone discipline (M0–M8)** — the contract-first ordering (canonical model → adapters → errors → transforms → pipeline → UNS) is a good template for sequencing the home-lab build.

## Extract from `engineering_drawing_business_case/` (EngiGraph) — the knowledge-graph layer

This is the design thinking for your eventual Neo4j contextualization. The *business pitch* you discard; the *graph architecture* you keep:

1. **The ontology foundation: ISO 15926 / DEXPI** (`Q9`) — a real, standards-based process-plant ontology instead of an ad-hoc graph schema. This is the single most valuable extract — it tells you *how to structure the Neo4j model* the design notes only sketch loosely.

# Project Charter — Industrial Data Harmonization & Contextualization Home Lab

**Status:** Authoritative project definition. Supersedes scattered framing in `docs/` and
`engineering_drawing_business_case/` (both to be archived once `README.md` and `AGENTS.md`
are updated to match this charter).

**Last updated:** 2026-05-28

---

## 1. Purpose

Build a **home lab that simulates a multi-site manufacturing enterprise** in which similar
operational realities are represented differently across sites, then:

1. **Harmonize** those disparate OT representations into a common enterprise language through
   a Sparkplug B / MQTT **Unified Namespace (UNS)**; and
2. **Contextualize** the harmonized data — tie it to assets, lines, sites, events, work orders,
   materials, and engineering topology — so it is meaningful to OT, IT, analytics, ML, ERP, and
   graph-based reasoning systems.

This is a **learning environment and architecture prototype**, not a product and not a
consulting deliverable. The explicit goal is to understand every layer of a modern industrial
data architecture at the bare-metal level *before* adopting enterprise-grade software that
abstracts those layers away.

### Guiding principle

> Only **Level 0 (the physical world)** is synthetic. Everything above it — PLC-facing
> structures, messaging, historian, analytics, ERP, knowledge graph, cloud — behaves like a
> real OT/IT stack assembled from open-source or free/community software.

---

## 2. The problem being simulated

The core problem is **not** collecting plant telemetry. It is that different sites, lines, and
machines represent the *same underlying reality* in different ways — because of local PLC naming
conventions, controller memory structures, brownfield integrations, differing tag taxonomies,
and uneven operational modeling. What should be enterprise-comparable data arrives as
site-specific, cryptic, inconsistent signals.

The lab deliberately manufactures this mess (same reality, different names per site), then proves
it can be conformed to one namespace and enriched into connected context.

The full problem has **two halves of contextualization**:

| Half | Problem | Lab plane |
|------|---------|-----------|
| **Operational data** | SCADA tags are cryptic, inconsistent, machine-unreadable | Harmonize (Plane 1) |
| **Engineering context** | Asset topology and relationships are trapped in static documents/silos | Contextualize (Plane 3) |

Clean operational data **plus** accurate engineering/relationship context = a complete foundation
for industrial AI. Neither is useful at full scale without the other.

---

## 3. The three planes

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PLANE 1 — HARMONIZE (OT)                                                 │
│   synthetic Level 0 → PLC-world disguise → Sparkplug B → UNS             │
│   units / status / timestamp normalization · per-field lineage           │
│   reference design: docs/ (ISHE patterns)                                │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ PLANE 2 — RECORD (Enterprise)                                            │
│   curated operational events → ERPNext (SAP-like)                        │
│   work orders · production confirmations · maintenance · inventory       │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ PLANE 3 — CONTEXTUALIZE (Knowledge)                                      │
│   UNS + ERP + asset topology → Neo4j knowledge graph → GraphRAG          │
│   ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned ontology · traversal & reasoning queries     │
│   reference design: engineering_drawing_business_case/ (EngiGraph)       │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 4. Layered technical architecture (ISA-95 view)

| Level | Role | Implementation |
|-------|------|----------------|
| **L0** | Synthetic & benchmark process reality | Python replay of benchmark datasets + generated signals |
| **L1/2** | PLC-world representation (brownfield realism) | OpenPLC and/or PLC-style tags (`N7:20`, `MW100`, `DB10.DBD4`, `FIC101_PV`) |
| **L3 — transport/UNS** | Harmonization backbone | MQTT broker (Mosquitto / EMQX OSS) + **Sparkplug B** |
| **L3 — OT consumers** | SCADA / storage / dashboards | Ignition Maker Edition, InfluxDB / TimescaleDB / QuestDB, Grafana |
| **L3/4 — analytics** | Streaming & analytical path | Kafka → Parquet/object store → DuckDB |
| **L4 — IT/cloud** | Cloud-shaped landing zone | floci (local AWS emulation: S3, Lambda, Kinesis, Glue, Athena, …) |
| **Cross-cutting — enterprise** | SAP-like business records | ERPNext |
| **Cross-cutting — knowledge** | Connected-context graph + reasoning | Neo4j + GraphRAG |
| **Cross-cutting — glue** | All custom logic | **Python** (Paho MQTT, PySparkplug, pandas, Pydantic, Neo4j driver) |

---

## 5. Implementation approach

The three architecture notes (`hand_built`, `umh_anchored`, `python_centric`) are **not three
competing projects**. They are phases / styles of the *same* architecture:

- **Build & learn phase → Hand-built + Python-centric.**
  Assemble every component explicitly so each boundary (where harmonization happens, what owns
  history vs. streaming, how OT and IT consume the same signal) is visible and testable. Python
  is the default implementation language and a *first-class UNS participant* (virtual sensors,
  Sparkplug publishers, enrichment nodes, inference services), not just glue.

- **Abstraction phase → UMH-anchored (later).**
  Once the internals are understood, United Manufacturing Hub Community can replace the
  hand-wired MQTT/Kafka/historian/modeling bundle. This is the "graduate to enterprise tooling"
  step — adopted *after* understanding what it abstracts.

Every component is chosen to be **upgrade-friendly**: OSS brokers → EMQX Enterprise/HiveMQ;
Ignition Maker → licensed Ignition; floci → real AWS; Python replay → real gateways — all without
invalidating the design.

---

## 6. Data strategy

Synthetic data is **layered, not random**. Benchmark datasets supply realistic multivariate
dynamics; Python fills operational/enterprise context and intentional messiness.

**Base datasets to replay:**
- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — machine/equipment behavior (motors, pumps, conveyors)
- **Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP)** — continuous multivariable process behavior + faults
- **Numenta Anomaly Benchmark (optional)** — extra anomaly-rich streams

**The three-stage name mapping table is the spine of the whole lab:**

| Stage | Example | Lives where |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| 1. Friendly source variable | `reactor1_feed_flow` | dataset / generator |
| 2. Site-specific PLC tag | `FIC101_PV` / `N7:20` (differs per site) | PLC-world layer |
| 3. Sparkplug metric + asset path | `Reactor1/FeedFlow` | UNS / harmonization |

This table also carries unit, range, cadence, asset class, site context, and the
work-order/batch/material/graph-entity IDs that later feed ERPNext and Neo4j. **Build this table
well and the rest is plumbing.**

**Six implementation layers** (from `synthetic_data_generation_notes.md`):
1. Ingestion · 2. Augmentation · 3. PLC mapping · 4. Sparkplug · 5. Context export · 6. Replay/orchestration

---

## 7. Design assets extracted from the archived docs

These patterns are **kept** and migrated into the home-lab design. The business/sales framing
around them is **discarded**.

### From `docs/` (ISHE — operational harmonization)

- **Canonical Pydantic model hierarchy** — `CanonicalTelemetry` → equipment-class submodels,
  `DataQuality`, `FieldLineage`, `DeadLetterEntry`, `UNSEnvelope`, `BirthCertificate`. This is the
  semantic target (stage 3) of the mapping table.
- **ISA-95 identity model** — Enterprise→Site→Area→Cell→EquipmentClass→EquipmentID.
  *Generalize* from O&G Well/ESP to the manufacturing Site/Area/Line/Cell/Asset hierarchy.
- **Per-field lineage discipline + config-driven YAML mapping** — direct implementation of the
  three-stage mapping table with provenance.
- **Transform primitives** — unit conversion, status normalization (unmapped → `Unknown`),
  timestamp coercion to UTC, cross-field data-quality flagging.
- **UNS semantics as a reference spec** — retained state, report-by-exception, birth certificates,
  wildcard matching, topic sanitization. ISHE implemented these *in-memory*; the home lab does the
  *real* version over MQTT/Sparkplug B, and uses ISHE's behavior as the **test oracle**.
- **Contract-first milestone discipline** — model → adapters → errors → transforms → pipeline → UNS.

### From `engineering_drawing_business_case/` (EngiGraph — engineering context)

- **Ontology foundation: ISO 15926 / DEXPI** — a standards-based process-plant ontology for the
  Neo4j model instead of an ad-hoc schema. (Highest-value extract for Plane 3.)
- **Multi-level ontology architecture** — Core Equipment → Process System → Facility → Cross-Facility;
  matches the "start simple, extend" philosophy.
- **Node/edge vocabulary** — Equipment, Instrument, Valve, Pipe, Control System /
  `connects-to`, `controls`, `isolates`, `inspects`, `belongs-to` — merged with the design notes'
  `PART_OF` / `HAS_METRIC` / `GENERATED_EVENT` / `FULFILLS_WORK_ORDER` / `CONSUMED_MATERIAL`.
- **GraphRAG pattern** — query the graph first; the LLM composes from retrieved graph data, not
  training data. Blueprint for the operator/engineer copilot.
- **Graph-algorithm use cases** — shortest-path (isolation routing), centrality (critical nodes),
  impact analysis. These are the demo queries that prove the graph is worth building.
- **Digital-thread framing** — topology ↔ SCADA tag ↔ ERP FLOC ↔ work order linkage.

### Deliberately NOT extracted

- All market sizing, revenue/TAM projections, persona pain tables, competitor matrices, named
  clients, and ER&I-challenge framing.
- The narrow O&G-only scope (Well/ESP; CygNet/Wonderware/Ignition specifics) — keep the *patterns*,
  swap the *examples* for manufacturing/multi-site assets.
- EngiGraph's CV/VLM P&ID-extraction pipeline (symbol detection, OCR, VLM). The home lab
  *synthesizes* graph topology directly, so it keeps only EngiGraph's **ontology + graph + query**
  layers, not the document-extraction layers.

---

## 8. Proposed build sequence

| Phase | Goal | Deliverable |
|-------|------|-------------|
| **0** | Skeleton | Repo layout, `pyproject.toml`, the 3-stage mapping table as config, one asset |
| **1** | Level 0 replay | Ingestion + augmentation over TEP / Industrial IoT, replay in time order |
| **2** | PLC disguise + Sparkplug | Mapping + Sparkplug publisher → Mosquitto/EMQX; verify NBIRTH/DBIRTH/NDATA |
| **3** | OT consume | InfluxDB historian + Grafana; optionally Ignition Maker as SCADA consumer |
| **4** | Multi-site | Clone asset template with *different* site tags → prove harmonization |
| **5** | Context | Context-export → ERPNext events + Neo4j graph (asset↔tag↔event↔work-order) |
| **6** | Loop closure | Python ML/inference publishes scores back into Sparkplug; floci cloud landing |
| **7** | Reasoning | GraphRAG over Neo4j for troubleshooting / lineage / impact queries |
| **Later** | Abstraction | Re-platform L3 backbone onto UMH Community |

Phases 0–4 are the core harmonization proof. Phases 5–7 are the contextualization story.

---

## 9. Design principles

- **Only Level 0 is synthetic** — everything above behaves like real software.
- **Preserve the PLC-world boundary** — never publish clean semantic names straight from Python;
  the cryptic → harmonized transition is the whole point.
- **Pydantic-first** — every data boundary is a validated model; no raw dicts cross layers.
- **Deterministic, reproducible transforms** — same input → same output.
- **Cross-source equivalence** — the same physical event represented differently across sites must
  produce identical harmonized output. This is the proof of harmonization.
- **Sparkplug B as the contract** — not plain JSON-over-MQTT; births, aliases, datatypes, lifecycle.
- **Harmonize before contextualize** — Neo4j/ERP consume the *harmonized* side, not raw values.
- **Config over code** — site mappings, status maps, unit factors, ontology are data.
- **Upgrade-friendly** — every OSS component has a credible paid/enterprise replacement path.
- **Python as a first-class participant** — not just glue; a native UNS node.

---

## 10. Scope

**In scope:** synthetic multi-site data; PLC-world disguise; Sparkplug B/MQTT UNS; historian +
dashboards; ERPNext enterprise integration; Neo4j knowledge graph + GraphRAG; floci cloud
emulation; Python ML/inference round-trip.

**Out of scope (for now):** real PLC/field hardware; live SCADA connections; document/P&ID
CV-VLM extraction; production security hardening; real cloud accounts; real ERP deployments
beyond ERPNext community.

---

## 11. Document map

| Document | Role |
|----------|------|
| `design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md` | **This file — authoritative project definition** |
| `design/uns_home_lab_notes.md` | Vision & high-level scope |
| `design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md` | Architecture option: hand-built |
| `design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md` | Architecture option: UMH-anchored (abstraction phase) |
| `design/python_centric_uns_notes.md` | Implementation philosophy: Python-centric |
| `design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md` | Data strategy & the 6-layer pipeline |
| `docs/` *(to be archived)* | Reference: ISHE harmonization patterns (Plane 1) |
| `engineering_drawing_business_case/` *(to be archived)* | Reference: EngiGraph ontology/graph patterns (Plane 3) |

---

## 12. Open decisions

1. **Manufacturing domain & asset roster** — which sites/lines/assets the lab simulates (working
   assumption: TEP-derived process units + Industrial-IoT-derived machines, cloned across ≥2 sites
   with divergent naming). *Needs confirmation — ripples through Planes 1 and 3.*
2. **Broker choice** — Mosquitto (minimal) vs. EMQX OSS (richer, clearer enterprise path).
3. **Historian choice** — InfluxDB vs. TimescaleDB vs. QuestDB.
4. **How literal the PLC layer is** — full OpenPLC runtime vs. Python-modeled controller tags.
5. **When ERPNext and Neo4j enter** — Phase 5 as planned, or earlier stubs.
</content>
</invoke>

- **Only Level 0 is synthetic** — everything above behaves like real software.
- **Preserve the PLC-world boundary** — never publish clean semantic names straight from Python;
  the cryptic → harmonized transition is the whole point.
- **Pydantic-first** — every data boundary is a validated model; no raw dicts cross layers.
- **Deterministic, reproducible transforms** — same input → same output.
- **Cross-source equivalence** — the same physical event represented differently across sites must
  produce identical harmonized output. This is the proof of harmonization.
- **Sparkplug B as the contract** — not plain JSON-over-MQTT; births, aliases, datatypes, lifecycle.
- **Harmonize before contextualize** — Neo4j/ERP consume the *harmonized* side, not raw values.
- **Config over code** — site mappings, status maps, unit factors, ontology are data.
- **Upgrade-friendly** — every OSS component has a credible paid/enterprise replacement path.
- **Python as a first-class participant** — not just glue; a native UNS node.

---

## 10. Scope

**In scope:** synthetic multi-site data; PLC-world disguise; Sparkplug B/MQTT UNS; historian +
dashboards; ERPNext enterprise integration; Neo4j knowledge graph + GraphRAG; floci cloud
emulation; Python ML/inference round-trip.

**Out of scope (for now):** real PLC/field hardware; live SCADA connections; document/P&ID
CV-VLM extraction; production security hardening; real cloud accounts; real ERP deployments
beyond ERPNext community.

---

---

## 12. Open decisions

1. **Manufacturing domain & asset roster** — which sites/lines/assets the lab simulates (working

   with divergent naming). *Needs confirmation — ripples through Planes 1 and 3.*

## Dataset Overview

The Tennessee Eastman Process simulation dataset is based on a simulated chemical process commonly used as a benchmark for fault detection and diagnosis algorithms, including data under various normal and faulty operating conditions generated by a dynamic model developed by Eastman Chemical Company.

## Variables Breakdown

### Manipulated Variables
The variables starting with xmv correspond to 11 manipulated variables (parameters that can be controlled by the person operating the process). These include manipulated variables such as flowrates, valve positions and the reaction agitator speed.

### Measured Variables
The variables starting with xmeas correspond to 41 measured variables of the TEP process. A total of 73 process variables of types flow (F), pressure (P), temperature (T), level (L) and chemical component concentration (A) are observed and measured.

## Total Variables

The dataset contains 52 total observation variables including all manipulated and measured variables.

## Fault Scenarios

Fault categories 1–7 are order variable faults, 8–12 are random variable faults, 13 is a slow drift fault in chemical reaction dynamics, 14–15 are corresponding viscous faults, 16–20 are unknown faults, and 21 is a constant position fault.

content.text:
Confirmed. Here's what those two anchor datasets actually represent:

## Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP)
- **Domain: chemical / petrochemical continuous process.** A dynamic simulation of a real Eastman Chemical Company process — reactor, condenser, compressor, separator, stripper; makes 2 products from 4 reactants.
- **Shape:** 52 observation variables (41 measured `xmeas` + 11 manipulated `xmv`), of types flow / pressure / temperature / level / composition — heavily **correlated, continuous, multivariate**, with control loops.
- **Faults:** 21 standard fault scenarios (step changes, random variation, slow drift, sticking valves, unknowns).
- This is **definitively a process-plant** dataset. Not flexible — it *is* a chemical process.

## Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic), canozensoy
- **Domain: generic rotating machinery / predictive maintenance.** Machine-level sensor monitoring, not tied to a specific industry.
- **Shape:** per-machine time series — `Machine_ID`, `Timestamp`, Temperature (°C), Pressure (kPa), Vibration (m/s²), humidity, power — with **failure / fault labels**. Discrete, machine-oriented, degradation-to-failure.
- This one **is** domain-flexible — those signals could be a pump, compressor, motor, conveyor in almost any plant.

## So, to your question — "Correct?"

**Yes, mostly** — dictating an arbitrary domain (say, automotive assembly) risks no readily available data, because you'd have to invent the physics.

**But with one refinement:** the data isn't a hard domain lock. Per your own pipeline (step 2: "map dataset variables to physical assets"), you *assign* physical meaning. The real constraint is the data's **statistical shape**, not its labels:
- TEP → continuous, correlated → **process units** (reactors, columns, utility loops)
- IIoT → discrete machine + failure → **rotating equipment** (pumps, compressors, motors)

## What domain they jointly imply

Put together, they naturally describe a **process-manufacturing plant** — most cleanly a **chemical / specialty-chemicals facility** that has both:
- continuous process units (from TEP), and
- rotating machines attached to them (from IIoT).

That's the path of least resistance: realistic, benchmark-backed, no fabrication. And conveniently, it lines up with the chemical/process framing already in your reference docs (TEP is a chemical benchmark; the EngiGraph/ISHE notes lean process-industry too).

So rather than *you* dictating the domain, **the data dictates it**: a multi-site chemical/process plant, where the same TEP process unit and the same IIoT machine type are cloned across ≥2 sites with deliberately divergent PLC naming — which is exactly the harmonization problem you want to prove.

That's already what the charter assumes in Open Decision #1. So my recommendation: **lock the domain as "multi-site process/chemical plant (TEP process units + IIoT rotating machines)"** and move on. Shall I update the charter to state that as decided rather than assumed, then proceed to the README/AGENTS rewrite?

- [Tennessee Eastman Process — Open Source Benchmark (KeepFloyding)](https://keepfloyding.github.io/posts/Ten-East-Proc-Intro/)
- [Tennessee Eastman dataset (GitHub, mv-per)](https://github.com/mv-per/tennessee-eastman-dataset)
- [Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic), Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/canozensoy/industrial-iot-dataset-synthetic)

# Industrial Data Harmonization & Contextualization Home Lab

A home lab that **simulates a multi-site process / specialty-chemicals manufacturer** in which
similar operational realities are represented differently across sites — then **harmonizes** those
disparate OT representations into a common enterprise language through a Sparkplug B / MQTT
**Unified Namespace (UNS)**, and **contextualizes** the result into a knowledge graph meaningful to
OT, IT, analytics, ML, ERP, and graph-based reasoning systems.

This is a **learning environment and architecture prototype** — built to understand every layer of
a modern industrial data stack at the bare-metal level *before* adopting enterprise software that
abstracts those layers away.

> **Authoritative project definition:** [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md).
> This README is a summary; the charter governs.

## The problem being simulated

Different sites, lines, and machines represent the *same underlying reality* differently — local
PLC naming, controller memory structures, brownfield integrations, divergent tag taxonomies. What
should be enterprise-comparable data arrives as site-specific, cryptic, inconsistent signals. The
lab deliberately manufactures this mess (same reality, different names per site), then proves it
can be conformed to one namespace and enriched into connected context.

## The three planes

| Plane | What it does | Key tech |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| **1 — Harmonize** (OT) | synthetic Level 0 → PLC-world disguise → Sparkplug B → UNS; unit/status/timestamp normalization + per-field lineage | OpenPLC, MQTT (Mosquitto/EMQX), Sparkplug B, Ignition, historian, Grafana |
| **2 — Record** (Enterprise) | curated operational events → SAP-like business records | ERPNext |
| **3 — Contextualize** (Knowledge) | UNS + ERP + asset topology → knowledge graph → reasoning | Neo4j (ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned ontology), GraphRAG |

## Guiding principle

> Only **Level 0 (the physical world)** is synthetic. Everything above — PLC-facing structures,
> messaging, historian, analytics, ERP, knowledge graph, cloud — behaves like a real OT/IT stack
> assembled from open-source or free/community software.

## Data strategy

The domain is **data-driven, not dictated**, so realistic data is always available:

- **Tennessee Eastman Process** — continuous chemical-process units (reactors, columns, loops)
- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — rotating machines (pumps, compressors, motors)

The same units/machines are cloned across ≥2 sites with deliberately divergent PLC naming. Physical
meaning is *assigned* at the mapping stage, anchored by the **three-stage name mapping table** —
`friendly variable → site-specific PLC tag → Sparkplug metric` — which is the spine of the lab.

## Implementation approach

The three architecture notes are **phases of one architecture**, not competing projects:

- **Build & learn → hand-built + Python-centric.** Wire every component explicitly so each boundary
  is visible; Python is a first-class UNS participant, not just glue.
- **Abstraction (later) → UMH-anchored.** Replace the hand-wired backbone with United Manufacturing
  Hub Community once the internals are understood.

Every component is upgrade-friendly (OSS broker → enterprise; Ignition Maker → licensed; floci →
real AWS) without invalidating the design.

## Documentation

| Document | Role |
|----------|------|
| [`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md`](design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md) | **Authoritative project definition** |
| [`design/uns_home_lab_notes.md`](design/uns_home_lab_notes.md) | Vision & high-level scope |
| [`design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md`](design/hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md) | Architecture: hand-built |
| [`design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md`](design/umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md) | Architecture: UMH-anchored (abstraction phase) |
| [`design/python_centric_uns_notes.md`](design/python_centric_uns_notes.md) | Implementation philosophy: Python-centric |
| [`design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md`](design/synthetic_data_generation_notes.md) | Data strategy & the 6-layer pipeline |

## Status

Pre-implementation — design and charter complete; build not yet started. See the charter's build
sequence (Phases 0–7) and open decisions.

## License

MIT
</content>

# SCADA Harmonization & Contextualization Service

A data harmonization pipeline that transforms heterogeneous industrial SCADA telemetry into standardized, ISA-95-aligned canonical messages for enterprise analytics and Unified Namespace (UNS) streaming architectures.

## Problem

Industrial telemetry systems suffer from:

- **Inconsistent naming** — camelCase, snake_case, hyphenated keys across sources
- **Varied JSON structures** — flat vs nested vs topic-based identity
- **Disparate units** — bpd vs m³/day, psi vs kPa, °F vs °C
- **Inconsistent status codes** — "P", "RUN", "Producing" mean the same thing
- **Unreliable timestamps** — ISO strings, epoch seconds, milliseconds, or missing
- **No contextual hierarchy** — lack of ISA-95 alignment

This fragmentation blocks cross-site KPI standardization, enterprise analytics, reliable streaming, M&A integration, and trustworthy AI applications.

## Solution

This service provides a centralized harmonization layer that:

1. Ingests events from multiple heterogeneous SCADA sources
2. Extracts ISA-95 contextual hierarchy (Enterprise → Site → Area → Cell → Equipment)
3. Normalizes units (m³/day → bpd, kPa → psi, °C → °F)
4. Standardizes status codes to a canonical enum
5. Validates telemetry constraints with strict Pydantic models
6. Emits canonical, enterprise-aligned events
7. Generates UNS-compatible topic structures
8. Provides full mapping lineage and explainability
9. Routes invalid events to dead-letter with structured errors

## Architecture

```
Input JSON → Source Adapter → Raw Extracted → Transform Layer → Canonical Model → UNS Envelope
```

See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for detailed design and [docs/PRD.md](docs/PRD.md) for full requirements.

## License

MIT

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI agents (and humans) working in this repository.

## Project overview

An **industrial data harmonization & contextualization home lab** that simulates a **multi-site
process / specialty-chemicals manufacturer**. It harmonizes deliberately-divergent OT data from
multiple sites into a common Sparkplug B / MQTT **Unified Namespace (UNS)**, then contextualizes
the result into a Neo4j knowledge graph. It is a **learning environment and architecture
prototype**, not a product — the goal is to understand each layer of a modern industrial data stack
before adopting enterprise software that abstracts it away.

The project is currently in a **pre-implementation state** (design/charter complete, no source code
yet).

## Authoritative source of truth

**`design/PROJECT_CHARTER.md` governs.** Read it first. If anything in this file or elsewhere
conflicts with the charter, the charter wins.

## Key documentation (all in `design/`)

- `PROJECT_CHARTER.md` — authoritative project definition (purpose, planes, architecture, build sequence, decisions)
- `uns_home_lab_notes.md` — vision & high-level scope
- `hand_built_sparkplug_uns_notes.md` — architecture option: hand-built (build/learn phase)
- `python_centric_uns_notes.md` — implementation philosophy: Python-centric
- `umh_anchored_sparkplug_uns_notes.md` — architecture option: UMH-anchored (later abstraction phase)
- `synthetic_data_generation_notes.md` — data strategy & the 6-layer synthetic pipeline

> **Archived references:** `docs/` (ISHE harmonization patterns) and `engineering_drawing_business_case/`
> (EngiGraph ontology/graph patterns) are **design references only**, not project definitions. The
> reusable *patterns* have been folded into the charter (§7); the business/market framing is discarded.
> They are slated for archival — do not treat them as current scope.

## The three planes

1. **Harmonize (OT)** — synthetic Level 0 → PLC-world disguise → Sparkplug B → UNS; unit/status/timestamp normalization + per-field lineage. *(reference patterns: ISHE / `docs/`)*
2. **Record (Enterprise)** — curated operational events → ERPNext (SAP-like).
3. **Contextualize (Knowledge)** — UNS + ERP + asset topology → Neo4j knowledge graph (ISO 15926 / DEXPI-aligned) → GraphRAG. *(reference patterns: EngiGraph / `engineering_drawing_business_case/`)*

## Architecture: data flow

```
L0 synthetic (TEP process + IIoT machines)
  → L1/2 PLC-world disguise (cryptic tags: N7:20, FIC101_PV — divergent per site)
  → L3 MQTT broker + Sparkplug B  ............... the UNS / harmonization contract
  → L3 OT consumers: Ignition (SCADA), historian (InfluxDB/Timescale), Grafana
  → L3/4 Kafka → Parquet/object store → DuckDB ... analytics path
  → L4 floci ..................................... local AWS emulation
  ── cross-cutting ──
  → ERPNext (enterprise records) · Neo4j (knowledge graph) · GraphRAG (reasoning)
```

All custom logic is **Python** (Paho MQTT, PySparkplug, pandas, Pydantic, Neo4j driver). Python is a
first-class UNS participant (virtual sensors, Sparkplug publishers, enrichment, inference), not glue.

## Critical design constraints

- **Only Level 0 is synthetic** — everything above behaves like real software.
- **Preserve the PLC-world boundary** — never publish clean semantic names straight from Python; the
  cryptic → harmonized transition is the whole point of the lab.
- **The three-stage mapping table is the spine** — `friendly variable → site-specific PLC tag →
  Sparkplug metric`, carrying unit, range, cadence, asset class, site context, and downstream
  ERP/graph IDs.
- **Pydantic-first** — every data boundary is a validated model; no raw dicts cross layers.
- **Deterministic, reproducible transforms** — same input → same output.
- **Cross-source equivalence** — the same physical event from different sites must produce identical
  harmonized output. This is the proof of harmonization.
- **Sparkplug B as the contract** — births, aliases, datatypes, lifecycle; not plain JSON-over-MQTT.
- **Harmonize before contextualize** — Neo4j/ERPNext consume the *harmonized* side, not raw values.
- **Config over code** — site mappings, status maps, unit factors, ontology are data.
- **Upgrade-friendly** — every OSS component has a credible enterprise replacement path.

## Domain & data

Multi-site process/specialty-chemicals plant. Anchor datasets (see charter §6):
- **Tennessee Eastman Process** — continuous process units (reactors, columns, loops).
- **Industrial IoT Dataset (Synthetic)** — rotating machines (pumps, compressors, motors).

Same units/machines cloned across ≥2 sites with divergent PLC naming. Physical meaning is *assigned*
at the mapping stage — the data's statistical shape, not its labels, is the constraint.

## Build sequence (see charter §8)

Phase 0 skeleton → 1 Level-0 replay → 2 PLC disguise + Sparkplug → 3 OT consume (historian/Grafana)
→ 4 multi-site (harmonization proof) → 5 context (ERPNext + Neo4j) → 6 loop closure (ML/inference +
floci) → 7 reasoning (GraphRAG) → later: re-platform onto UMH.

## Build and development commands

No build tooling exists yet (pre-implementation). When implementation begins it will be a Python
project (Pydantic v2, pandas, paho-mqtt, PySparkplug). Update this section once `pyproject.toml`
lands.
</content>
